subject: social-studies
title: Research Design and the Arc of Inquiry
essential_question: What makes a research question worth asking and actually answerable?
performance_task: Produce a reviewed research proposal with a compelling question, supporting questions, candidate sources, methods, and ethical safeguards.
anchor_sources: C3 Framework for Social Studies State Standards (National Council for the Social Studies)
Michigan K-12 Social Studies Standards, Arc of Inquiry, grades 9-12 (Michigan Department of Education)

subject: social-studies
title: Historiography and Contested Interpretation
essential_question: Why do capable historians reach different conclusions from the same evidence?
topics: identifying an author's argument and evidence
comparing competing accounts of one event
performance_task: Write a historiographic analysis comparing at least three published interpretations of one event, attributing each argument accurately.
anchor_sources: Peer-reviewed historical journals available through public and university library access
Published review essays and bibliographic guides (Library of Congress research guides)

subject: social-studies
title: Advanced Source Criticism and Evidence Standards
essential_question: How do you establish that a source is what it claims to be?
topics: distinguishing primary and secondary sources at scale
performance_task: Build an annotated source dossier documenting provenance, reliability, and corroboration for every source in your capstone.
anchor_sources: Archival finding aids and provenance documentation (National Archives and Library of Congress)
Published citation standards (Chicago Manual of Style; Modern Language Association handbook)

subject: social-studies
title: Comparative Government and Constitutional Design
essential_question: What difference does institutional design make to how a society governs itself?
performance_task: Compare two governmental systems against a shared criterion set and defend an evaluative conclusion.
anchor_sources: National constitutional texts (Constitute Project, constituteproject.org)
Charter of the United Nations and member state documentation (United Nations Digital Library)

subject: social-studies
title: Geospatial and Quantitative Analysis for Social Science
essential_question: What can maps and data honestly show, and where do they mislead?
performance_task: Produce a map-and-data analysis that states its methods, limitations, and uncertainty explicitly.
anchor_sources: United States Census Bureau data and geographic files (census.gov)
Federal Reserve Economic Data series (fred.stlouisfed.org)
United Nations population and development statistics (United Nations Digital Library)

subject: social-studies
title: Applied Economics and Policy Analysis
essential_question: How do you compare policy options when every option has costs?
performance_task: Write a policy memo with alternatives, stated criteria, distributional analysis, and a defended recommendation.
anchor_sources: Congressional Budget Office cost estimates and reports (cbo.gov)
Government Accountability Office program evaluations (gao.gov)
Federal Register rules and notices (federalregister.gov)

subject: social-studies
title: Scoping the Capstone Issue: Contemporary Global and National Investigation
essential_question: Is the issue you have chosen actually researchable with the evidence you can obtain?
topics: historical roots of a current issue
performance_task: Scope your own capstone issue: narrow it to a researchable question, trace its historical roots, and test it against reporting and official sources from at least three countries, naming the evidence you cannot obtain.
anchor_sources: United Nations reports and resolutions (United Nations Digital Library)
Congressional Research Service reports (crsreports.congress.gov)

subject: social-studies
title: Public Discourse, Deliberation, and Argument from Evidence
essential_question: How do you argue well with someone you believe is wrong?
topics: representing opposing positions at their strongest
rules of evidence in public debate
revising a position under new evidence
performance_task: Lead and document a deliberation in which you accurately represent a position you do not personally hold.
anchor_sources: Congressional hearing transcripts (congress.gov and govinfo.gov)
Public rulemaking comment dockets (regulations.gov)

subject: social-studies
title: Capstone: Independent Research, Civic Action, and Public Defense
essential_question: Can you defend your own conclusion to someone who has not agreed to be persuaded?
topics: reflection and transfer beyond the course
performance_task: Complete the senior capstone: an independent research argument, a documented civic action, and a defense that answers unrehearsed questions.
source_focus: the learner's own annotated source dossier
public records relevant to the action
anchor_sources: The learner's annotated source dossier assembled in Unit 3
Public records and correspondence generated by the learner's civic action
